title: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of endocarditis: Developed by the task force on the management of endocarditis of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Endorsed by the European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery (EACTS) and the European Association of Nuclear Medicine (EANM)

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic prophylaxis in patients with cardiovascular diseases undergoing oro-dental procedures at increased risk for infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Use general infection-prevention measures for people at high or intermediate risk of infective endocarditis (IE).

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic prophylaxis in patients with cardiovascular diseases undergoing oro-dental procedures at increased risk for infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Provide antibiotic prophylaxis for high-risk oro-dental procedures in patients with previous IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic prophylaxis in patients with cardiovascular diseases undergoing oro-dental procedures at increased risk for infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Provide dental antibiotic prophylaxis for surgically implanted prosthetic valves or material used in surgical valve repair.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic prophylaxis in patients with cardiovascular diseases undergoing oro-dental procedures at increased risk for infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Provide dental antibiotic prophylaxis for transcatheter aortic or pulmonary valve prostheses.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic prophylaxis in patients with cardiovascular diseases undergoing oro-dental procedures at increased risk for infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Provide dental antibiotic prophylaxis for unrepaired cyanotic congenital heart disease and for repaired congenital disease with palliative shunts, conduits, or other prostheses. After surgical repair without residual defects or a valve prosthesis, prophylaxis applies only during the first 6 months.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic prophylaxis in patients with cardiovascular diseases undergoing oro-dental procedures at increased risk for infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Provide dental antibiotic prophylaxis for patients with a ventricular assist device.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic prophylaxis in patients with cardiovascular diseases undergoing oro-dental procedures at increased risk for infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider dental antibiotic prophylaxis after transcatheter mitral or tricuspid valve repair.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic prophylaxis in patients with cardiovascular diseases undergoing oro-dental procedures at increased risk for infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Dental antibiotic prophylaxis may be considered after heart transplantation.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic prophylaxis in patients with cardiovascular diseases undergoing oro-dental procedures at increased risk for infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Do not routinely provide dental antibiotic prophylaxis to other patients at low risk of IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for infective endocarditis prevention in high-risk patients
recommendations.text: For patients at high IE risk, provide prophylaxis before dental extraction, oral surgery, or procedures manipulating gingival or periapical tissue.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for infective endocarditis prevention in high-risk patients
recommendations.text: For patients at high IE risk, systemic antibiotic prophylaxis may be considered for invasive diagnostic or therapeutic procedures involving the respiratory, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, skin, or musculoskeletal systems.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for infective endocarditis prevention in cardiac procedures
recommendations.text: Before elective cardiac surgery or transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), screen for nasal Staphylococcus aureus carriage and treat identified carriers.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for infective endocarditis prevention in cardiac procedures
recommendations.text: Give perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis before implantation of a cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED).

recommendations.section: Recommendations for infective endocarditis prevention in cardiac procedures
recommendations.text: Use appropriate skin-site asepsis for CIED implantation.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for infective endocarditis prevention in cardiac procedures
recommendations.text: Give perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis when implanting a prosthetic valve or other intravascular foreign material.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for infective endocarditis prevention in cardiac procedures
recommendations.text: Use aseptic measures in catheterization laboratories to prevent healthcare-associated IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for infective endocarditis prevention in cardiac procedures
recommendations.text: Consider eliminating potential septic foci, including dental infection, at least 2 weeks before implantation of a prosthetic valve or other intracardiac/intravascular foreign material, unless the intervention is urgent.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for infective endocarditis prevention in cardiac procedures
recommendations.text: Before TAVI or other transcatheter valve procedures, consider prophylaxis covering common skin organisms, including Enterococcus species and S. aureus.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for infective endocarditis prevention in cardiac procedures
recommendations.text: Do not perform systematic local decolonization without screening for S. aureus.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the Endocarditis Team
recommendations.text: Treat complicated IE early in a Heart Valve Centre with an Endocarditis Team and immediate cardiac-surgical capability.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the Endocarditis Team
recommendations.text: Uncomplicated IE may be managed in a referring centre when it maintains early, regular communication with a Heart Valve Centre Endocarditis Team.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of echocardiography in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Use transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) as the initial imaging test in suspected IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of echocardiography in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Perform transoesophageal echocardiography (TOE) when IE is suspected and TTE is negative or nondiagnostic.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of echocardiography in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Perform TOE when IE is suspected in a patient with a prosthetic valve or intracardiac device.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of echocardiography in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Repeat TTE and/or TOE within 5–7 days when the initial examination is negative or inconclusive and clinical suspicion remains high.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of echocardiography in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Perform TOE even when TTE is positive, except for isolated right-sided native-valve IE with good-quality, unequivocal TTE findings.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of echocardiography in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider echocardiography in S. aureus or Enterococcus faecalis bacteraemia and in some Streptococcus bacteraemias.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of echocardiography in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Repeat TTE and/or TOE promptly if a new complication is suspected, including a new murmur, embolism, persistent fever or bacteraemia, heart failure, abscess, or atrioventricular block.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of echocardiography in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Perform TOE in clinically stable IE before switching from intravenous to oral antibiotic treatment.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of echocardiography in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider repeat TTE/TOE during uncomplicated IE to detect silent complications and monitor vegetation size; choose timing according to initial findings, organism, and treatment response.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of echocardiography in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Use intraoperative echocardiography for every patient undergoing IE surgery.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of echocardiography in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: At completion of antibiotics, obtain TTE and/or TOE to assess cardiac and valve morphology and function in patients who did not undergo valve surgery.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of computed tomography, nuclear imaging, and magnetic resonance in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Use cardiac CT angiography (CTA) in possible native-valve IE to detect valvular lesions and help confirm IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of computed tomography, nuclear imaging, and magnetic resonance in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Use FDG-PET/CT angiography and cardiac CTA in possible prosthetic-valve IE to detect lesions and confirm the diagnosis.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of computed tomography, nuclear imaging, and magnetic resonance in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Use cardiac CTA to detect perivalvular or periprosthetic complications when echocardiography is inconclusive in native- or prosthetic-valve IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of computed tomography, nuclear imaging, and magnetic resonance in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: In symptomatic native- or prosthetic-valve IE, use brain and whole-body CT, FDG-PET/CT, and/or MRI to detect peripheral lesions or add diagnostic criteria.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of computed tomography, nuclear imaging, and magnetic resonance in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider labelled-white-cell SPECT/CT when prosthetic-valve IE is strongly suspected, echocardiography is negative or inconclusive, and PET/CT is unavailable.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of computed tomography, nuclear imaging, and magnetic resonance in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: FDG-PET/CT angiography may be considered to help confirm possible CIED-related IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the role of computed tomography, nuclear imaging, and magnetic resonance in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Brain and whole-body CT, FDG-PET/CT, and/or MRI screening may be considered in asymptomatic native- or prosthetic-valve IE to detect peripheral lesions.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to oral streptococci and Streptococcus gallolyticus group
recommendations.text: For penicillin-susceptible oral streptococci or the Streptococcus gallolyticus group, use penicillin G, amoxicillin, or ceftriaxone for 4 weeks in native-valve IE or 6 weeks in prosthetic-valve IE. Source dosing: Adults: penicillin G 12–18 million units/day IV in 4–6 doses or continuous infusion; amoxicillin 12 g/day IV in 4–6 doses; or ceftriaxone 2 g/day IV once daily. Children: penicillin G 200,000 units/kg/day IV in 4–6 doses; amoxicillin 200–300 mg/kg/day IV in 4–6 doses (maximum 12 g/day); or ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg IV once daily. The source advises starting at the lower end of dose ranges and increasing if needed. Duration is 4 weeks for native-valve IE and 6 weeks for prosthetic-valve IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to oral streptococci and Streptococcus gallolyticus group
recommendations.text: For uncomplicated native-valve IE caused by penicillin-susceptible oral streptococci/S. gallolyticus with normal renal function, a 2-week course of penicillin G, amoxicillin, or ceftriaxone plus gentamicin is recommended. This short regimen does not apply to prosthetic-valve IE. Source dosing: Adults: penicillin G 12–18 million units/day IV in 4–6 doses or continuous infusion, amoxicillin 12 g/day IV in 4–6 doses, or ceftriaxone 2 g/day IV once daily, each with gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM once daily. Children: penicillin G 200,000 units/kg/day IV in 4–6 divided doses (corrected), amoxicillin 200–300 mg/kg/day IV in 4–6 doses (maximum 12 g/day), or ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg IV once daily, each with gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM in one or three equal doses. Start at the lower end of ranges and increase as needed. All drugs are given for 2 weeks, only for uncomplicated native-valve IE with normal renal function. Gentamicin footnote: maximum 240 mg/day; higher doses increase nephrotoxicity. Check renal function and serum concentrations at least weekly as specified in the source. With once-daily dosing, target trough below 1 mg/L and peak about 10–12 mg/L 1 hour after injection.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to oral streptococci and Streptococcus gallolyticus group
recommendations.text: For beta-lactam allergy with penicillin-susceptible oral streptococcal/S. gallolyticus IE, use vancomycin for 4 weeks in native-valve IE or 6 weeks in prosthetic-valve IE. Source dosing: Adults: vancomycin 30 mg/kg/day IV in 2 doses. Children: vancomycin 30 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 equal doses. Treat native-valve IE for 4 weeks and prosthetic-valve IE for 6 weeks. Vancomycin table footnote: trough 10–15 mg/L; some experts use 45–60 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 doses to target trough 15–20 mg/L. Do not exceed 2 g/day without serum-level monitoring and adjustment; the printed footnote specifies a peak of 30–45 micrograms/mL 1 hour after infusion.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to oral streptococci and Streptococcus gallolyticus group
recommendations.text: For native-valve IE from oral streptococci/S. gallolyticus requiring increased penicillin exposure or resistant to penicillin, use penicillin G, amoxicillin, or ceftriaxone for 4 weeks with gentamicin during the first 2 weeks. Source dosing: Adults: penicillin G 24 million units/day IV in 4–6 doses or continuous infusion, amoxicillin 12 g/day IV in 4–6 doses (corrected), or ceftriaxone 2 g/day IV once daily, for 4 weeks; add gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM once daily for the first 2 weeks. This resistant/increased-exposure row does not print a separate paediatric dosing schedule. Gentamicin footnote: maximum 240 mg/day; higher doses increase nephrotoxicity. Check renal function and serum concentrations at least weekly as specified in the source. With once-daily dosing, target trough below 1 mg/L and peak about 10–12 mg/L 1 hour after injection.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to oral streptococci and Streptococcus gallolyticus group
recommendations.text: For prosthetic-valve IE from oral streptococci/S. gallolyticus requiring increased penicillin exposure or resistant to penicillin, use penicillin G, amoxicillin, or ceftriaxone for 6 weeks with gentamicin during the first 2 weeks. Source dosing: Adults: penicillin G 24 million units/day IV in 4–6 doses or continuous infusion, amoxicillin 12 g/day IV in 4–6 doses (corrected), or ceftriaxone 2 g/day IV once daily, for 6 weeks; add gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM once daily for the first 2 weeks. This resistant/increased-exposure row does not print a separate paediatric dosing schedule. Gentamicin footnote: maximum 240 mg/day; higher doses increase nephrotoxicity. Check renal function and serum concentrations at least weekly as specified in the source. With once-daily dosing, target trough below 1 mg/L and peak about 10–12 mg/L 1 hour after injection.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to oral streptococci and Streptococcus gallolyticus group
recommendations.text: For beta-lactam-allergic native-valve IE from oral streptococci/S. gallolyticus requiring increased penicillin exposure or resistant to penicillin, use vancomycin for 4 weeks. Source dosing: Adults and children: vancomycin 30 mg/kg/day IV in 2 doses for 4 weeks. The paediatric schedule in this specific row is twice daily. Vancomycin table footnote: trough 10–15 mg/L; some experts use 45–60 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 doses to target trough 15–20 mg/L. Do not exceed 2 g/day without serum-level monitoring and adjustment; the printed footnote specifies a peak of 30–45 micrograms/mL 1 hour after infusion.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to oral streptococci and Streptococcus gallolyticus group
recommendations.text: For beta-lactam-allergic prosthetic-valve IE from oral streptococci/S. gallolyticus requiring increased penicillin exposure or resistant to penicillin, use vancomycin for 6 weeks with gentamicin during the first 2 weeks. Source dosing: Adults and children: vancomycin 30 mg/kg/day IV in 2 doses for 6 weeks, plus gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM once daily during the first 2 weeks. Gentamicin footnote: maximum 240 mg/day; higher doses increase nephrotoxicity. Check renal function and serum concentrations at least weekly as specified in the source. With once-daily dosing, target trough below 1 mg/L and peak about 10–12 mg/L 1 hour after injection. Vancomycin table footnote: trough 10–15 mg/L; some experts use 45–60 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 doses to target trough 15–20 mg/L. Do not exceed 2 g/day without serum-level monitoring and adjustment; the printed footnote specifies a peak of 30–45 micrograms/mL 1 hour after infusion.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to Staphylococcus spp.
recommendations.text: For methicillin-susceptible staphylococcal native-valve IE, use (flu)cloxacillin or cefazolin for 4–6 weeks. Source dosing: Adults: (flu)cloxacillin 12 g/day IV in 4–6 doses or cefazolin 6 g/day IV in 3 doses. Children: (flu)cloxacillin 200–300 mg/kg/day IV in 4–6 equal doses or cefazolin 100 mg/kg/day IV in 3–4 doses (maximum 6 g/day; corrected). Treat for 4–6 weeks. Cefazolin/ceftaroline substitution for cloxacillin is limited by the source footnotes to non-immediate penicillin hypersensitivity; cloxacillin is not recommended with penicillin allergy.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to Staphylococcus spp.
recommendations.text: For methicillin-susceptible staphylococcal prosthetic-valve IE, use (flu)cloxacillin or cefazolin plus rifampin for at least 6 weeks, with gentamicin during the first 2 weeks. Source dosing: Adults: (flu)cloxacillin 12 g/day IV in 4–6 doses or cefazolin 6 g/day IV in 3 doses. Children: (flu)cloxacillin 200–300 mg/kg/day IV in 4–6 equal doses or cefazolin 100 mg/kg/day IV in 3–4 doses (maximum 6 g/day; corrected). Adults also receive rifampin 900 mg/day IV/orally in 3 equal doses and gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM in one preferred daily dose or 2 doses. Children also receive rifampin 20 mg/kg/day IV/orally in 3 doses (maximum 900 mg/day) and gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM in one preferred daily dose or 2 doses. Rifampin and the primary antibiotic continue for at least 6 weeks; gentamicin is limited to the first 2 weeks. Cefazolin/ceftaroline substitution for cloxacillin is limited by the source footnotes to non-immediate penicillin hypersensitivity; cloxacillin is not recommended with penicillin allergy. Gentamicin footnote: maximum 240 mg/day; higher doses increase nephrotoxicity. Check renal function and serum concentrations at least weekly as specified in the source. With once-daily dosing, target trough below 1 mg/L and peak about 10–12 mg/L 1 hour after injection.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to Staphylococcus spp.
recommendations.text: For penicillin-allergic patients with methicillin-susceptible staphylococcal native-valve IE, use cefazolin for 4–6 weeks. Source dosing: Adults: cefazolin 6 g/day IV in 3 doses. Children: cefazolin 100 mg/kg/day IV in 3–4 doses, maximum 6 g/day (corrected). Treat for 4–6 weeks. Cefazolin/ceftaroline substitution for cloxacillin is limited by the source footnotes to non-immediate penicillin hypersensitivity; cloxacillin is not recommended with penicillin allergy.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to Staphylococcus spp.
recommendations.text: For penicillin-allergic patients with methicillin-susceptible staphylococcal prosthetic-valve IE, use cefazolin and rifampin for at least 6 weeks with gentamicin during the first 2 weeks. Source dosing: Adults: cefazolin 6 g/day IV in 3 doses. Children: cefazolin 100 mg/kg/day IV in 3–4 doses, maximum 6 g/day (corrected). Adults also receive rifampin 900 mg/day IV/orally in 3 equal doses and gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM in one preferred daily dose or 2 doses. Children also receive rifampin 20 mg/kg/day IV/orally in 3 doses (maximum 900 mg/day) and gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM in one preferred daily dose or 2 doses. Rifampin and the primary antibiotic continue for at least 6 weeks; gentamicin is limited to the first 2 weeks. Cefazolin/ceftaroline substitution for cloxacillin is limited by the source footnotes to non-immediate penicillin hypersensitivity; cloxacillin is not recommended with penicillin allergy. Gentamicin footnote: maximum 240 mg/day; higher doses increase nephrotoxicity. Check renal function and serum concentrations at least weekly as specified in the source. With once-daily dosing, target trough below 1 mg/L and peak about 10–12 mg/L 1 hour after injection.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to Staphylococcus spp.
recommendations.text: For beta-lactam-allergic patients with methicillin-susceptible staphylococcal native-valve IE, daptomycin combined with ceftaroline or fosfomycin may be considered. Source dosing: Adults: daptomycin 10 mg/kg/day IV once daily plus either ceftaroline 1,800 mg/day IV in 3 doses or fosfomycin 8–12 g/day IV in 4 doses. This row does not specify a separate paediatric regimen or its own treatment duration. Cefazolin/ceftaroline substitution for cloxacillin is limited by the source footnotes to non-immediate penicillin hypersensitivity; cloxacillin is not recommended with penicillin allergy. High-dose ceftaroline can cause leucopenia after 2 weeks. Fosfomycin’s sodium load can precipitate acute heart failure in patients with heart failure.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to Staphylococcus spp.
recommendations.text: For beta-lactam-allergic patients with methicillin-susceptible staphylococcal prosthetic-valve IE, a daptomycin-based combination with ceftaroline, fosfomycin, or gentamicin and rifampin may be considered. The source regimen uses rifampin for at least 6 weeks and gentamicin for 2 weeks; select the combination with the Endocarditis Team. Source dosing: The printed adult schedule is daptomycin 10 mg/kg/day IV once daily; ceftaroline 1,800 mg/day IV in 3 doses or fosfomycin 8–12 g/day IV in 4 doses; rifampin 900 mg/day IV/orally in 3 equal doses; and gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM in one preferred daily dose or 2 doses. The source wording permits daptomycin combined with ceftaroline, fosfomycin, or gentamicin with rifampin for at least 6 weeks, with gentamicin for 2 weeks. The combination syntax is ambiguous; confirm the intended regimen with the Endocarditis Team. No separate paediatric regimen is printed. Cefazolin/ceftaroline substitution for cloxacillin is limited by the source footnotes to non-immediate penicillin hypersensitivity; cloxacillin is not recommended with penicillin allergy. Gentamicin footnote: maximum 240 mg/day; higher doses increase nephrotoxicity. Check renal function and serum concentrations at least weekly as specified in the source. With once-daily dosing, target trough below 1 mg/L and peak about 10–12 mg/L 1 hour after injection. High-dose ceftaroline can cause leucopenia after 2 weeks. Fosfomycin’s sodium load can precipitate acute heart failure in patients with heart failure.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to Staphylococcus spp.
recommendations.text: For methicillin-resistant staphylococcal native-valve IE, use vancomycin for 4–6 weeks. Source dosing: Adults: vancomycin 30–60 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 doses. Children: vancomycin 30 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 equal doses. Treat for 4–6 weeks. Vancomycin table footnote: trough 10–15 mg/L; some experts use 45–60 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 doses to target trough 15–20 mg/L. Do not exceed 2 g/day without serum-level monitoring and adjustment; the printed footnote specifies a peak of 30–45 micrograms/mL 1 hour after infusion. The accompanying MRSA discussion (Section 7.7) recommends AUC/MIC 400–600 mg·h/L, assuming MIC 1 mg/L, within 48 hours, because trough-based escalation risks nephrotoxicity; consider another treatment when MIC exceeds 1 mg/L.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to Staphylococcus spp.
recommendations.text: For methicillin-resistant staphylococcal prosthetic-valve IE, use vancomycin plus rifampin for at least 6 weeks, with gentamicin during the first 2 weeks. Source dosing: Adults: vancomycin 30–60 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 doses, rifampin 900–1,200 mg/day IV/orally in 2–3 doses, and gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM in one preferred daily dose or 2 doses. Children: vancomycin 30 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 equal doses, rifampin 20 mg/kg/day IV/orally in 3 doses (maximum 900 mg/day), and gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM in one preferred daily dose or 2 doses. Continue vancomycin/rifampin for at least 6 weeks and gentamicin for the first 2 weeks. Gentamicin footnote: maximum 240 mg/day; higher doses increase nephrotoxicity. Check renal function and serum concentrations at least weekly as specified in the source. With once-daily dosing, target trough below 1 mg/L and peak about 10–12 mg/L 1 hour after injection. Vancomycin table footnote: trough 10–15 mg/L; some experts use 45–60 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 doses to target trough 15–20 mg/L. Do not exceed 2 g/day without serum-level monitoring and adjustment; the printed footnote specifies a peak of 30–45 micrograms/mL 1 hour after infusion. The accompanying MRSA discussion (Section 7.7) recommends AUC/MIC 400–600 mg·h/L, assuming MIC 1 mg/L, within 48 hours, because trough-based escalation risks nephrotoxicity; consider another treatment when MIC exceeds 1 mg/L.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to Staphylococcus spp.
recommendations.text: For methicillin-resistant staphylococcal native-valve IE, daptomycin combined with cloxacillin, ceftaroline, or fosfomycin may be considered. Source dosing: Adults: daptomycin 10 mg/kg/day IV once daily plus cloxacillin 12 g/day IV in 6 doses, ceftaroline 1,800 mg/day IV in 3 doses, or fosfomycin 8–12 g/day IV in 4 doses. The source does not print a separate paediatric schedule or duration for this alternative combination. Cefazolin/ceftaroline substitution for cloxacillin is limited by the source footnotes to non-immediate penicillin hypersensitivity; cloxacillin is not recommended with penicillin allergy. High-dose ceftaroline can cause leucopenia after 2 weeks. Fosfomycin’s sodium load can precipitate acute heart failure in patients with heart failure.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to Enterococcus spp.
recommendations.text: For native-valve enterococcal IE without high-level aminoglycoside resistance, use ampicillin or amoxicillin with ceftriaxone for 6 weeks, or use an ampicillin/amoxicillin regimen with gentamicin limited to 2 weeks. Source dosing: Adults: ampicillin or amoxicillin 12 g/day IV in 4–6 doses, plus ceftriaxone 4 g/day IV in 2 doses or gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM once daily. Children: ampicillin or amoxicillin 200–300 mg/kg/day IV in 4–6 doses (maximum 12 g/day), plus ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg IV in 2 doses or gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM in 3 equal doses. The ceftriaxone combination is given for 6 weeks; the gentamicin component is given for 2 weeks. The source row does not separately state the total ampicillin/amoxicillin duration for the gentamicin option. Gentamicin footnote: maximum 240 mg/day; higher doses increase nephrotoxicity. Check renal function and serum concentrations at least weekly as specified in the source. With once-daily dosing, target trough below 1 mg/L and peak about 10–12 mg/L 1 hour after injection. Section 7.8 states that ampicillin–ceftriaxone is effective for E. faecalis and not effective against E. faecium; do not generalize the dual-beta-lactam regimen to all enterococci.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to Enterococcus spp.
recommendations.text: For prosthetic-valve or complicated native-valve enterococcal IE, or symptoms lasting more than 3 months, without high-level aminoglycoside resistance, use ampicillin/amoxicillin with ceftriaxone for 6 weeks or an ampicillin/amoxicillin regimen with gentamicin limited to 2 weeks. Source dosing: Adults: ampicillin or amoxicillin 12 g/day IV in 4–6 doses, plus ceftriaxone 4 g/day IV in 2 doses or gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM once daily. Children: ampicillin or amoxicillin 200–300 mg/kg/day IV in 4–6 doses (maximum 12 g/day), plus ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg/day IV in 2 doses or gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM in 3 equal doses. The ceftriaxone combination is given for 6 weeks; the gentamicin component is given for 2 weeks. The source row does not separately state the total ampicillin/amoxicillin duration for the gentamicin option. Gentamicin footnote: maximum 240 mg/day; higher doses increase nephrotoxicity. Check renal function and serum concentrations at least weekly as specified in the source. With once-daily dosing, target trough below 1 mg/L and peak about 10–12 mg/L 1 hour after injection. Section 7.8 states that ampicillin–ceftriaxone is effective for E. faecalis and not effective against E. faecium; do not generalize the dual-beta-lactam regimen to all enterococci.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to Enterococcus spp.
recommendations.text: For native- or prosthetic-valve enterococcal IE with high-level aminoglycoside resistance, use ampicillin or amoxicillin plus ceftriaxone for 6 weeks. Source dosing: Adults: ampicillin or amoxicillin 12 g/day IV in 4–6 doses plus ceftriaxone 4 g/day IV/IM in 2 doses. Children: ampicillin or amoxicillin 200–300 mg/kg/day IV in 4–6 doses (maximum 12 g/day) plus ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg IV/IM in 2 doses. Treat for 6 weeks. For high-level gentamicin resistance with streptomycin susceptibility, the source footnote offers streptomycin 15 mg/kg/day in 2 equal doses in place of gentamicin; it does not specify a route in that footnote. Section 7.8 states that ampicillin–ceftriaxone is effective for E. faecalis and not effective against E. faecium; do not generalize the dual-beta-lactam regimen to all enterococci.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to Enterococcus spp.
recommendations.text: For beta-lactam-resistant E. faecium IE, use vancomycin for 6 weeks with gentamicin during the first 2 weeks. Source dosing: Adults: vancomycin 30 mg/kg/day IV in 2 doses for 6 weeks plus gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM once daily for the first 2 weeks. Children: vancomycin 30 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 equal doses plus gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM once daily, with the same durations. When beta-lactam resistance arises from beta-lactamase, the footnote advises ampicillin–sulbactam or amoxicillin–clavulanate in place of the corresponding unprotected agent; PBP5-mediated resistance calls for a vancomycin-based regimen. Gentamicin footnote: maximum 240 mg/day; higher doses increase nephrotoxicity. Check renal function and serum concentrations at least weekly as specified in the source. With once-daily dosing, target trough below 1 mg/L and peak about 10–12 mg/L 1 hour after injection.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis due to Enterococcus spp.
recommendations.text: For vancomycin-resistant enterococcal IE, use high-dose daptomycin with a beta-lactam (ampicillin, ertapenem, or ceftaroline) or fosfomycin. Source dosing: Adults: daptomycin 10–12 mg/kg/day IV once daily plus ampicillin 12 g/day IV in 4–6 doses, ertapenem 2 g/day IV/IM once daily, ceftaroline 1,800 mg/day IV in 3 doses, or fosfomycin 12 g/day IV in 4 doses. Children: age-adjusted daptomycin 10–12 mg/kg/day IV once daily; ampicillin 200–300 mg/kg/day IV in 4–6 doses (maximum 12 g/day); fosfomycin 2–3 g/day IV in one dose; ceftaroline 24–36 mg/kg/day in 3 doses (route not printed in that paediatric cell); or ertapenem 1 g/day IV/IM once daily, with the source specifying 15 mg/kg/dose twice daily, maximum 500 mg/dose, below age 12. The paediatric fosfomycin entry has no weight band; confirm specialist dosing rather than extrapolating. No duration is specified for these daptomycin combinations. For multiresistant infection the footnote lists daptomycin 10 mg/kg/day with ampicillin 200 mg/kg/day IV in 4–6 doses, ertapenem 2 g/day IV, ceftaroline 600 mg IV every 8 hours, or fosfomycin 3 g IV every 6 hours; this ampicillin option differs from the main corrected fixed adult dose. Other alternatives are linezolid 600 mg IV/orally twice daily for at least 8 weeks with haematological monitoring, or quinupristin–dalfopristin 7.5 mg/kg three times daily for at least 8 weeks (route not printed; inactive against E. faecalis). Consult infectious-disease specialists for regimen selection and source-dose discrepancies. High-dose ertapenem carries seizure risk.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic regimens for initial empirical treatment of infective endocarditis (before pathogen identification) a
recommendations.text: For initial empirical treatment of community-acquired native-valve IE or late prosthetic-valve IE (at least 12 months after surgery), consider ampicillin plus ceftriaxone, or ampicillin plus (flu)cloxacillin and gentamicin. Source dosing: Adults: ampicillin 12 g/day IV in 4–6 doses with either ceftriaxone 4 g/day IV/IM in 2 doses, or (flu)cloxacillin 12 g/day IV in 4–6 doses plus gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM once daily. Children: ampicillin 200–300 mg/kg/day IV in 4–6 doses (maximum 12 g/day), with ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg IV/IM once daily, or (flu)cloxacillin 200–300 mg/kg/day IV in 4–6 equal doses plus gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM in 3 equal doses. Gentamicin footnote: maximum 240 mg/day; higher doses increase nephrotoxicity. Check renal function and serum concentrations at least weekly as specified in the source. With once-daily dosing, target trough below 1 mg/L and peak about 10–12 mg/L 1 hour after injection. If cultures remain negative without clinical response, consider blood-culture-negative pathogens and broaden the workup/treatment; molecular diagnosis is an option when surgery is undertaken. The source assigns no fixed empirical-course duration: narrow treatment to the identified organism and susceptibility.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic regimens for initial empirical treatment of infective endocarditis (before pathogen identification) a
recommendations.text: For initial empirical treatment of early prosthetic-valve IE (less than 12 months after surgery) or healthcare-associated IE, vancomycin or daptomycin combined with gentamicin and rifampin may be considered. Paediatric rifampin is 20 mg/kg/day IV/orally in 3 doses, maximum 900 mg/day. Source dosing: Adults: vancomycin 30 mg/kg/day IV in 2 doses or daptomycin 10 mg/kg/day IV once daily, together with gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM once daily and rifampin 900–1,200 mg IV/orally in 2–3 doses. The rifampin cell omits “per day”; the surrounding daily-dose schedule implies a total daily dose, but the printed omission is retained here rather than silently corrected. Children: vancomycin 40 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 equal doses, gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM in 3 equal doses, and rifampin 20 mg/kg/day IV/orally in 3 doses (maximum 900 mg/day). No paediatric daptomycin dose is listed in this empirical table. Gentamicin footnote: maximum 240 mg/day; higher doses increase nephrotoxicity. Check renal function and serum concentrations at least weekly as specified in the source. With once-daily dosing, target trough below 1 mg/L and peak about 10–12 mg/L 1 hour after injection. Vancomycin table footnote: trough 10–15 mg/L; some experts use 45–60 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 doses to target trough 15–20 mg/L. Do not exceed 2 g/day without serum-level monitoring and adjustment; the printed footnote specifies a peak of 30–45 micrograms/mL 1 hour after infusion. If cultures remain negative without clinical response, consider blood-culture-negative pathogens and broaden the workup/treatment; molecular diagnosis is an option when surgery is undertaken. The source assigns no fixed empirical-course duration: narrow treatment to the identified organism and susceptibility.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for antibiotic regimens for initial empirical treatment of infective endocarditis (before pathogen identification) a
recommendations.text: For penicillin-allergic patients receiving empirical treatment for community-acquired native-valve IE or late prosthetic-valve IE, cefazolin or vancomycin combined with gentamicin may be considered. Paediatric cefazolin is 100 mg/kg/day IV in 3–4 doses, maximum 6 g/day. Source dosing: Adults: cefazolin 6 g/day IV in 3 doses or vancomycin 30 mg/kg/day IV in 2 doses, each with gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM once daily. Children: cefazolin 100 mg/kg/day IV in 3–4 doses (maximum 6 g/day; corrected) or vancomycin 40 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 equal doses, each with gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV/IM in 3 equal doses. Cefazolin/ceftaroline substitution for cloxacillin is limited by the source footnotes to non-immediate penicillin hypersensitivity; cloxacillin is not recommended with penicillin allergy. Gentamicin footnote: maximum 240 mg/day; higher doses increase nephrotoxicity. Check renal function and serum concentrations at least weekly as specified in the source. With once-daily dosing, target trough below 1 mg/L and peak about 10–12 mg/L 1 hour after injection. Vancomycin table footnote: trough 10–15 mg/L; some experts use 45–60 mg/kg/day IV in 2–3 doses to target trough 15–20 mg/L. Do not exceed 2 g/day without serum-level monitoring and adjustment; the printed footnote specifies a peak of 30–45 micrograms/mL 1 hour after infusion. If cultures remain negative without clinical response, consider blood-culture-negative pathogens and broaden the workup/treatment; molecular diagnosis is an option when surgery is undertaken. The source assigns no fixed empirical-course duration: narrow treatment to the identified organism and susceptibility.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for outpatient antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider outpatient IV or oral therapy for clinically stable left-sided IE caused by Streptococcus species, E. faecalis, S. aureus, or coagulase-negative staphylococci after at least 10 days of appropriate IV antibiotics (or at least 7 days after cardiac surgery), when TOE shows no abscess or valve abnormality requiring surgery.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for outpatient antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Do not use outpatient parenteral therapy for IE with highly difficult-to-treat organisms, Child–Pugh B/C cirrhosis, severe cerebral emboli, untreated large extracardiac abscesses, valve complications or other conditions requiring surgery, severe postoperative complications, or injection-drug-use-related IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the main indications of surgery in infective endocarditis (native valve endocarditis and prosthetic valve endocarditis) a
recommendations.text: Perform emergency surgery, within 24 hours, for aortic or mitral native-/prosthetic-valve IE with severe acute regurgitation, obstruction, or fistula causing refractory pulmonary oedema or cardiogenic shock.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the main indications of surgery in infective endocarditis (native valve endocarditis and prosthetic valve endocarditis) a
recommendations.text: Perform urgent surgery, generally within 3–5 days, for aortic or mitral native-/prosthetic-valve IE with severe acute regurgitation or obstruction causing heart-failure symptoms or echocardiographic evidence of poor haemodynamic tolerance.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the main indications of surgery in infective endocarditis (native valve endocarditis and prosthetic valve endocarditis) a
recommendations.text: Perform urgent surgery for locally uncontrolled infection, including abscess, false aneurysm, fistula, enlarging vegetation, prosthetic dehiscence, or new atrioventricular block.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the main indications of surgery in infective endocarditis (native valve endocarditis and prosthetic valve endocarditis) a
recommendations.text: Operate for fungal IE or infection with multiresistant organisms; choose urgent or nonurgent timing according to haemodynamic status.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the main indications of surgery in infective endocarditis (native valve endocarditis and prosthetic valve endocarditis) a
recommendations.text: Consider urgent surgery when blood cultures remain positive for more than 1 week or sepsis persists despite appropriate antibiotics and adequate control of metastatic infection.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the main indications of surgery in infective endocarditis (native valve endocarditis and prosthetic valve endocarditis) a
recommendations.text: Consider urgent surgery for prosthetic-valve IE caused by S. aureus or non-HACEK Gram-negative bacteria.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the main indications of surgery in infective endocarditis (native valve endocarditis and prosthetic valve endocarditis) a
recommendations.text: Perform urgent surgery for aortic or mitral native-/prosthetic-valve IE with persistent vegetation at least 10 mm after one or more embolic events despite appropriate antibiotics.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the main indications of surgery in infective endocarditis (native valve endocarditis and prosthetic valve endocarditis) a
recommendations.text: Perform urgent surgery for IE with a vegetation at least 10 mm when another indication for surgery is present.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the main indications of surgery in infective endocarditis (native valve endocarditis and prosthetic valve endocarditis) a
recommendations.text: Urgent surgery may be considered for aortic or mitral IE with vegetation at least 10 mm even without severe valve dysfunction or clinical embolism when surgical risk is low.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the treatment of neurological complications of infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Obtain brain CT or MR angiography when an infective cerebral aneurysm is suspected in IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the treatment of neurological complications of infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Use neurosurgical or endovascular treatment for large infective cerebral aneurysms, aneurysms that continue growing despite optimal antibiotics, or ruptured infective cerebral aneurysms.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the treatment of neurological complications of infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider catheter angiography when noninvasive vascular imaging is negative but suspicion of an infective cerebral aneurysm remains.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the treatment of neurological complications of infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Mechanical thrombectomy may be considered for embolic stroke from IE when timely expertise is available.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the treatment of neurological complications of infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Do not use thrombolysis for embolic stroke caused by IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for pacemaker implantation in patients with complete atrioventricular block and infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider immediate epicardial pacemaker implantation during valve surgery for IE with complete atrioventricular block when there is preoperative conduction disease, S. aureus infection, aortic-root abscess, tricuspid involvement, or previous valve surgery.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for patients with musculoskeletal manifestations of infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Use MRI or PET/CT for suspected spondylodiscitis or vertebral osteomyelitis complicating IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for patients with musculoskeletal manifestations of infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Use TTE/TOE to exclude IE in spondylodiscitis or septic arthritis with positive blood cultures for typical IE organisms.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for patients with musculoskeletal manifestations of infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider antibiotics beyond 6 weeks for IE-related osteoarticular infection caused by difficult-to-treat organisms such as S. aureus or Candida, or complicated by severe vertebral destruction or abscess.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for pre-operative coronary anatomy assessment in patients requiring surgery for infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: For haemodynamically stable patients with aortic-valve vegetations who need surgery and have high coronary artery disease risk, use high-resolution coronary CTA.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for pre-operative coronary anatomy assessment in patients requiring surgery for infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Use invasive coronary angiography before heart surgery in patients at high coronary disease risk who do not have aortic-valve vegetations.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for pre-operative coronary anatomy assessment in patients requiring surgery for infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: In an emergency, consider proceeding to valve surgery without preoperative coronary-anatomy assessment, irrespective of coronary disease risk.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for pre-operative coronary anatomy assessment in patients requiring surgery for infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: In selected patients with known coronary disease or high risk of obstructive disease, invasive coronary angiography may be considered despite aortic-valve vegetations.

recommendations.section: Indications and timing of cardiac surgery after neurological complications in active infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: After a transient ischaemic attack, perform indicated cardiac surgery without delay.

recommendations.section: Indications and timing of cardiac surgery after neurological complications in active infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: After stroke, do not delay indicated surgery for heart failure, uncontrolled infection, abscess, or persistent high embolic risk when the patient is not comatose and CT/MRI has excluded cerebral haemorrhage.

recommendations.section: Indications and timing of cardiac surgery after neurological complications in active infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: After intracranial haemorrhage, consider delaying cardiac surgery for more than 1 month if feasible, with frequent clinical and imaging reassessment.

recommendations.section: Indications and timing of cardiac surgery after neurological complications in active infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: With intracranial haemorrhage and instability from heart failure, uncontrolled infection, or persistent high embolic risk, consider urgent or emergency surgery after weighing the prospect of meaningful neurological recovery.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for post-discharge follow-up
recommendations.text: During follow-up, educate patients about recurrence prevention and individualized risk, emphasizing dental health.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for post-discharge follow-up
recommendations.text: Provide addiction treatment after injection-drug-use-related IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for post-discharge follow-up
recommendations.text: Consider individualized cardiac rehabilitation, including exercise, in clinically stable patients.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for post-discharge follow-up
recommendations.text: Psychosocial care may be integrated into follow-up, including anxiety/depression screening and referral for appropriate psychological treatment.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for prosthetic valve endocarditis
recommendations.text: Treat early prosthetic-valve IE occurring within 6 months of valve surgery with repeat valve replacement and complete debridement.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for cardiovascular implanted electronic device-related infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Give prophylactic antibiotics covering S. aureus for CIED implantation.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for cardiovascular implanted electronic device-related infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Use both TTE and TOE to assess suspected CIED-related IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for cardiovascular implanted electronic device-related infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Remove the complete CIED system without delay in definite CIED-related IE while providing initial empirical antibiotics.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for cardiovascular implanted electronic device-related infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Collect at least three sets of blood cultures before promptly starting empirical treatment for CIED infection covering methicillin-resistant staphylococci and Gram-negative bacteria.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for cardiovascular implanted electronic device-related infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: When reimplantation is necessary after extraction for CIED-related IE, use a distant site and delay as long as feasible until infection signs resolve and blood cultures remain negative for at least 72 hours without vegetations, or at least 2 weeks when vegetations were present.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for cardiovascular implanted electronic device-related infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider complete CIED extraction for valvular IE even without definite lead involvement, taking the organism and valve-surgery requirement into account.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for cardiovascular implanted electronic device-related infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider complete system removal for possible CIED-related IE with persistent occult Gram-positive bacteraemia or fungaemia despite antimicrobial therapy.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for cardiovascular implanted electronic device-related infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider extending antibiotics to 4–6 weeks after device extraction when CIED-related IE has septic emboli or prosthetic valves.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for cardiovascular implanted electronic device-related infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: An antibiotic envelope may be considered during CIED reimplantation in selected patients at high infection risk.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for cardiovascular implanted electronic device-related infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Complete system removal may be considered for possible CIED-related IE with persistent or relapsing occult Gram-negative bacteraemia after antibiotics.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for cardiovascular implanted electronic device-related infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: A 2-week antibiotic course after extraction may be considered for non-S. aureus CIED-related IE when there is no valve involvement or lead vegetation, follow-up cultures are negative, and septic emboli are absent.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for cardiovascular implanted electronic device-related infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Do not remove a CIED solely for one positive blood culture without other clinical evidence of infection.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the surgical treatment of right-sided infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Operate for right-sided IE despite appropriate antibiotics when acute severe tricuspid regurgitation causes right-ventricular dysfunction unresponsive to diuretics.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the surgical treatment of right-sided infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Operate for right-sided IE despite appropriate antibiotics when persistent vegetation and recurrent pulmonary emboli cause respiratory insufficiency requiring ventilatory support.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the surgical treatment of right-sided infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Operate for right-sided IE despite appropriate antibiotics when residual tricuspid vegetation exceeds 20 mm after recurrent septic pulmonary emboli.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the surgical treatment of right-sided infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Operate for right-sided IE despite appropriate antibiotics when left-heart structures are also involved.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the surgical treatment of right-sided infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider tricuspid valve repair rather than replacement when feasible.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the surgical treatment of right-sided infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider surgery for right-sided IE with persistent bacteraemia or sepsis after at least 1 week of appropriate antibiotics.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the surgical treatment of right-sided infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider prophylactic placement of an epicardial pacing lead during tricuspid valve surgery.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the surgical treatment of right-sided infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Aspiration debulking of right-atrial septic masses may be considered in selected patients at high surgical risk.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the use of antithrombotic therapy in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Interrupt antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy for major bleeding, including intracranial haemorrhage, in IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the use of antithrombotic therapy in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: For intracranial haemorrhage in a patient with a mechanical valve, consider restarting unfractionated heparin as soon as possible after multidisciplinary discussion.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the use of antithrombotic therapy in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: In the absence of stroke, consider replacing oral anticoagulation with closely monitored unfractionated heparin when surgery is likely, such as in S. aureus IE.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for the use of antithrombotic therapy in infective endocarditis
recommendations.text: Do not administer thrombolytic therapy to patients with IE.

recommendations.section: General prevention measures
recommendations.text: Encourage twice-daily tooth cleaning, with professional dental cleaning and review at least every 6 months for high-risk patients and annually for others.

recommendations.section: General prevention measures
recommendations.text: Maintain skin hygiene and optimize treatment of chronic skin disorders.

recommendations.section: General prevention measures
recommendations.text: Disinfect wounds.

recommendations.section: General prevention measures
recommendations.text: Treat identified bacterial infection foci with appropriate curative antibiotics.

recommendations.section: General prevention measures
recommendations.text: Advise against self-prescribing antibiotics.

recommendations.section: General prevention measures
recommendations.text: Use strict infection-control practices for procedures that carry infection risk.

recommendations.section: General prevention measures
recommendations.text: Discourage body piercing and tattoos in patients at increased IE risk.

recommendations.section: General prevention measures
recommendations.text: Avoid unnecessary infusion catheters and invasive procedures.

recommendations.section: General prevention measures
recommendations.text: Follow central- and peripheral-cannula care bundles consistently.

recommendations.section: Dental antibiotic prophylaxis regimens
recommendations.text: For high-risk dental procedures without penicillin/ampicillin allergy, the oral amoxicillin prophylaxis dose is 2 g for adults or 50 mg/kg for children (maximum 2 g), given once 30–60 minutes before the procedure.

recommendations.section: Dental antibiotic prophylaxis regimens
recommendations.text: Without penicillin/ampicillin allergy, parenteral ampicillin prophylaxis is 2 g IM/IV for adults or 50 mg/kg IM/IV for children (maximum 2 g), once 30–60 minutes before the procedure.

recommendations.section: Dental antibiotic prophylaxis regimens
recommendations.text: Without penicillin/ampicillin allergy, parenteral cefazolin or ceftriaxone prophylaxis is 1 g IM/IV for adults or 50 mg/kg IM/IV for children (maximum 1 g), once 30–60 minutes before the procedure. The corrected paediatric maximum is 1 g.

recommendations.section: Dental antibiotic prophylaxis regimens
recommendations.text: For penicillin/ampicillin allergy without previous anaphylaxis, angioedema, or urticaria, cephalexin is an oral option: adults 2 g; children 50 mg/kg (maximum 2 g), once 30–60 minutes before the procedure. An equivalent first- or second-generation oral cephalosporin is an alternative.

recommendations.section: Dental antibiotic prophylaxis regimens
recommendations.text: For penicillin/ampicillin allergy, azithromycin or clarithromycin prophylaxis is 500 mg orally for adults or 15 mg/kg for children (maximum 500 mg), once 30–60 minutes before the procedure.

recommendations.section: Dental antibiotic prophylaxis regimens
recommendations.text: For penicillin/ampicillin allergy, doxycycline prophylaxis is 100 mg orally for adults. Table 6 lists 2.2 mg/kg orally below 45 kg and 100 mg above 45 kg, once 30–60 minutes before the procedure; it does not specify the exactly-45-kg boundary.

recommendations.section: Dental antibiotic prophylaxis regimens
recommendations.text: For penicillin/ampicillin allergy without previous anaphylaxis, angioedema, or urticaria, cefazolin or ceftriaxone prophylaxis is 1 g IM/IV for adults or 50 mg/kg IM/IV for children (maximum 1 g), once 30–60 minutes before the procedure. Avoid cephalosporins after those immediate allergy reactions.

recommendations.section: Proposed treatment of blood-culture-negative IE
recommendations.text: For Brucella IE, the source proposes oral doxycycline plus cotrimoxazole and rifampin for at least 3–6 months; an initial aminoglycoside may be added. Assess response with antibody titre (target below 1:60). These rare-pathogen regimens require infectious-disease input because optimal duration is uncertain.

recommendations.section: Proposed treatment of blood-culture-negative IE
recommendations.text: For Coxiella burnetii IE, the proposed regimen is doxycycline plus hydroxychloroquine for more than 18 months, with hydroxychloroquine-level monitoring and serological response assessment (phase-I IgG below 1:400 and IgA/IgM below 1:50).

recommendations.section: Proposed treatment of blood-culture-negative IE
recommendations.text: For Bartonella IE, the source proposes doxycycline for 4 weeks plus gentamicin for the first 2 weeks. Use specialist-guided aminoglycoside dosing and monitoring; the narrative table contains an inconsistent printed gentamicin unit, so no dose is reproduced here.

recommendations.section: Proposed treatment of blood-culture-negative IE
recommendations.text: For Legionella IE, proposed options are levofloxacin for at least 6 weeks or clarithromycin IV for 2 weeks followed by oral treatment for 4 weeks, with rifampin. The optimal regimen is unknown.

recommendations.section: Proposed treatment of blood-culture-negative IE
recommendations.text: For Mycoplasma IE, levofloxacin for at least 6 months is a proposed regimen; optimal treatment is unknown.

recommendations.section: Proposed treatment of blood-culture-negative IE
recommendations.text: For Tropheryma whipplei IE, the source proposes doxycycline plus hydroxychloroquine for at least 18 months, with drug-level monitoring; add sulfadiazine for CNS involvement. Alternative initial IV ceftriaxone or penicillin G plus streptomycin followed by prolonged cotrimoxazole is described, but treatment and duration remain empirical and trimethoprim itself lacks activity.

recommendations.section: Outpatient antibiotic eligibility and treatment phases
recommendations.text: Consider outpatient IV or oral treatment only with clinical stability, a stable home setting (preferably with a cohabiting caregiver), and self-care capacity or available home healthcare.

recommendations.section: Outpatient antibiotic eligibility and treatment phases
recommendations.text: Supplementary outpatient exclusions include heart failure; severe regurgitation, vegetation over 10 mm, progression or local complications; neurological involvement; renal impairment; malabsorption; and injection drug use. Apply the graded exclusions in Recommendation Table 11 as well.

recommendations.section: Outpatient antibiotic eligibility and treatment phases
recommendations.text: During the initial 0–2 weeks, outpatient IV treatment may be considered for native-valve IE from oral streptococci or S. gallolyticus.

recommendations.section: Outpatient antibiotic eligibility and treatment phases
recommendations.text: During the initial phase, oral step-down may be considered only after at least 10 days of IV treatment.

recommendations.section: Outpatient antibiotic eligibility and treatment phases
recommendations.text: For early native-valve IE outpatient transition, Table S8 requires more than 10 days of IV therapy after admission or surgery, no highly difficult-to-treat organism, cultures negative at 72 hours, TOE excluding severe aortic regurgitation or prosthetic dysfunction, and no anticoagulation problems.

recommendations.section: Outpatient antibiotic eligibility and treatment phases
recommendations.text: For early prosthetic-valve IE outpatient transition, Table S8 requires more than 10 days of IV therapy; oral streptococci, S. gallolyticus, or E. faecalis; no surgical indication; cultures negative at 72 hours; reassuring TOE; and no anticoagulation problems.

recommendations.section: Outpatient antibiotic eligibility and treatment phases
recommendations.text: For early CIED outpatient transition, Table S8 requires more than 7 days of IV treatment after uncomplicated lead extraction performed within the first admission week, no highly difficult-to-treat organism, no pocket infection, negative cultures at 72 hours after reimplantation, and normal echocardiography.

recommendations.section: Outpatient antibiotic eligibility and treatment phases
recommendations.text: Beyond week 2, oral step-down may be considered after at least 10 days of IV therapy for Streptococcus species, E. faecalis, S. aureus, or coagulase-negative staphylococci.

recommendations.section: Outpatient antibiotic eligibility and treatment phases
recommendations.text: For delayed native-valve IE outpatient transition, Table S8 specifies more than 3 weeks of IV treatment, no highly difficult-to-treat organism, negative cultures at 72 hours, reassuring TOE, no anticoagulation problems or severe sequelae/complications, and no need for daily or complex wound care.

recommendations.section: Outpatient antibiotic eligibility and treatment phases
recommendations.text: For delayed prosthetic-valve IE outpatient transition, Table S8 specifies more than 3 weeks of IV treatment after admission or surgery, surgery completed without severe complications or difficult-to-treat infection, negative cultures at 72 hours, reassuring TOE, no anticoagulation problems, and no need for daily or complex wound care.

recommendations.section: Outpatient antibiotic eligibility and treatment phases
recommendations.text: For delayed CIED outpatient transition, Table S8 describes more than 2 weeks of IV therapy after removal/reimplantation in cases with right-sided vegetations over 2 cm, associated left-sided IE (apply native/prosthetic-valve criteria), or late/complicated extraction. Exclude highly difficult organisms, pocket infection, persistent cultures, abnormal echocardiography, severe sequelae/complications, and daily/complex wound-care needs.

recommendations.section: Source-listed oral step-down combinations
recommendations.text: For penicillin- and methicillin-susceptible S. aureus/coagulase-negative staphylococci, source-listed oral pairs are amoxicillin–rifampin, amoxicillin–fusidic acid, moxifloxacin–rifampin, linezolid–rifampin, or linezolid–fusidic acid. Use only after meeting outpatient stability and source-specific eligibility criteria. Source oral schedules: amoxicillin/dicloxacillin 1 g four times daily; rifampin/linezolid 600 mg twice daily; fusidic acid 750 mg twice daily; moxifloxacin 400 mg once daily. Use only the two agents in the selected source-listed pair, after the outpatient eligibility criteria are met.

recommendations.section: Source-listed oral step-down combinations
recommendations.text: For methicillin-susceptible S. aureus/coagulase-negative staphylococci, source-listed oral pairs are dicloxacillin–rifampin, dicloxacillin–fusidic acid, moxifloxacin–rifampin, linezolid–rifampin, or linezolid–fusidic acid. This is a regimen table, not a new graded recommendation. Source oral schedules: amoxicillin/dicloxacillin 1 g four times daily; rifampin/linezolid 600 mg twice daily; fusidic acid 750 mg twice daily; moxifloxacin 400 mg once daily. Use only the two agents in the selected source-listed pair, after the outpatient eligibility criteria are met.

recommendations.section: Source-listed oral step-down combinations
recommendations.text: For methicillin-resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci, the listed oral combinations are linezolid with fusidic acid or rifampin; the table does not extend these options to methicillin-resistant S. aureus. Source oral schedules: amoxicillin/dicloxacillin 1 g four times daily; rifampin/linezolid 600 mg twice daily; fusidic acid 750 mg twice daily; moxifloxacin 400 mg once daily. Use only the two agents in the selected source-listed pair, after the outpatient eligibility criteria are met.

recommendations.section: Source-listed oral step-down combinations
recommendations.text: For E. faecalis, listed oral pairs are amoxicillin–moxifloxacin, amoxicillin–linezolid, amoxicillin–rifampin, linezolid–moxifloxacin, or linezolid–rifampin. Source oral schedules: amoxicillin/dicloxacillin 1 g four times daily; rifampin/linezolid 600 mg twice daily; fusidic acid 750 mg twice daily; moxifloxacin 400 mg once daily. Use only the two agents in the selected source-listed pair, after the outpatient eligibility criteria are met.

Use only the two agents in the selected source-listed pair, after the outpatient eligibility criteria are met.

recommendations.section: Perioperative neurological-risk mitigation after stroke
recommendations.text: For preoperative anaemia, consider a low transfusion threshold, infection treatment, and IV iron when appropriate.

recommendations.section: Perioperative neurological-risk mitigation after stroke
recommendations.text: For cardiopulmonary bypass, keep activated clotting time in the therapeutic range and optimize preoperative coagulopathy.

recommendations.section: Perioperative neurological-risk mitigation after stroke
recommendations.text: Loss of pulsatility during cardiopulmonary bypass is listed as an unmodifiable contributor to neurological risk.

recommendations.section: Perioperative neurological-risk mitigation after stroke
recommendations.text: Maintain an appropriate mean systemic pressure during anaesthesia/bypass when cerebral autoregulation may be impaired.

recommendations.section: Perioperative neurological-risk mitigation after stroke
recommendations.text: Avoid systemic hypotension or hypertension during surgery and early postoperative care by maintaining appropriate mean systemic pressure.

recommendations.section: Perioperative neurological-risk mitigation after stroke
recommendations.text: For reduced haematocrit and blood oxygen content, use a low perioperative transfusion threshold and avoid further haemodilution.

recommendations.section: Perioperative neurological-risk mitigation after stroke
recommendations.text: Maintain carbon-dioxide levels within range and avoid more than mild hypothermia unless aortic-arch surgery or prolonged cross-clamping is expected.

recommendations.section: Perioperative neurological-risk mitigation after stroke
recommendations.text: Reduce micro-/macroembolism by limiting cardiac manipulation before aortic clamping, controlling surgical debris during valve debridement, and thorough deairing before separation from bypass.

recommendations.section: Perioperative neurological-risk mitigation after stroke
recommendations.text: Avoid unnecessary volume expansion and haemodilution; consider haemofiltration during bypass for preoperative hypervolaemia or oedema.

recommendations.section: Perioperative neurological-risk mitigation after stroke
recommendations.text: Address coagulopathy with meticulous surgical technique, haemofiltration, and active correction of haemostatic disturbances even without overt bleeding.

recommendations.section: Perioperative neurological-risk mitigation after stroke
recommendations.text: The complexity of reconstruction and duration of cardiopulmonary bypass are listed as unmodifiable contributors to neurological risk.

recommendations.section: Perioperative neurological-risk mitigation after stroke
recommendations.text: A need for intra-aortic balloon counterpulsation or other temporary mechanical circulatory support is listed as an unmodifiable contributor to neurological risk.

recommendations.section: IE in intensive care
recommendations.text: Urgently discuss any IE patient requiring intensive-care admission with the Endocarditis Team; management decisions should be multidisciplinary.

recommendations.section: IE in intensive care
recommendations.text: For critically ill patients, consider preoperative haemodynamic optimization and goal-directed treatment, including vasoactive drugs or mechanical circulatory support when appropriate.

recommendations.section: IE with congenital heart disease
recommendations.text: In congenital heart disease with persistent fever or infection features, consider IE and obtain multiple blood cultures before antibiotics. A negative echocardiogram does not exclude IE in complex anatomy or prosthetic material; additional TOE or advanced imaging may be needed.

recommendations.section: IE with congenital heart disease
recommendations.text: Provide multidisciplinary IE care in a specialized congenital-heart centre with congenital imaging/surgery, infectious-disease, and intensive-care expertise. Surgical indications follow those for acquired-heart-disease IE.

recommendations.section: IE with rheumatic heart disease
recommendations.text: Investigate patients with rheumatic heart disease for IE when fever or a new/changing murmur occurs; prevention and access to diagnostic and surgical care are particularly relevant in endemic settings.

recommendations.section: IE during pregnancy
recommendations.text: Consider IE in pregnancy with unexplained fever, cardiac signs, a new/changing murmur, or septic embolic features. Add obstetric, gynaecological, and neonatal specialists to the Endocarditis Team and formulate a diagnostic/treatment plan promptly.

recommendations.section: IE during pregnancy
recommendations.text: Do not delay indicated urgent cardiac surgery solely because of pregnancy; weigh maternal and fetal risks with the multidisciplinary team.

recommendations.section: IE in immunocompromised patients
recommendations.text: In people living with HIV, apply the same surgical indications used for patients without HIV.

recommendations.section: IE in immunocompromised patients
recommendations.text: In neutropenia, use the usual antibiotic and surgical principles while considering antibiotic adverse effects that may worsen neutropenia, including those of cloxacillin or ceftaroline.

recommendations.section: Antithrombotic treatment context
recommendations.text: IE itself is not an indication to start antiplatelets or anticoagulation, and no evidence supports starting them to treat or prevent IE-associated stroke. Review pre-existing indications, bleeding, and surgery plans within the Endocarditis Team.

recommendations.section: Non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis
recommendations.text: Suspect non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) with systemic embolism and a predisposing condition such as cancer, antiphospholipid antibodies, or systemic lupus erythematosus; use echocardiography to distinguish NBTE from infection and other masses.

recommendations.section: Non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis
recommendations.text: Treat the underlying NBTE cause to reduce recurrence. Consider anticoagulation after balancing bleeding risk; source-listed options are low-molecular-weight heparin, unfractionated heparin, or a vitamin K antagonist. The guideline identifies no supporting data for direct oral anticoagulants in NBTE.

recommendations.section: Non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis
recommendations.text: Consider surgery for NBTE with severe valve dysfunction or large vegetations; the overall surgical role remains uncertain.

recommendations.section: IE with malignancy
recommendations.text: Discuss valve-surgery indications for IE with cancer in an Endocarditis Team that includes a cardio-oncologist and the treating oncologist, weighing operative risks, expected benefit, and cancer prognosis.

recommendations.section: Patient-centred care and shared decisions
recommendations.text: Involve patients, families, and caregivers throughout diagnosis, treatment, and recovery; incorporate the patient’s preferences and values, coordinated care, understandable information, comfort, and emotional support.

recommendations.section: Patient-centred care and shared decisions
recommendations.text: During diagnosis and active treatment, reduce procedural/symptom discomfort and distress, provide timely information about options and prognosis, and preserve continuity, personal autonomy, and family access when feasible.

recommendations.section: Patient-centred care and shared decisions
recommendations.text: Decide on outpatient antibiotics jointly with the patient and family, accounting for preferences, transportation, and self-care ability; teach them how to recognize progression or recurrence.

recommendations.section: Patient-centred care and shared decisions
recommendations.text: Develop a recovery plan collaboratively with patients and caregivers and review it soon after discharge, adjusting to physical and psychological recovery.

recommendations.section: Patient-centred care and shared decisions
recommendations.text: Tailor exercise to assessed functional capacity and address the patient’s and family’s education and psychosocial needs, including recurrence prevention.

recommendations.section: Patient-centred care and shared decisions
recommendations.text: For patients without close relatives or support networks, consider peer support, mentors, or telephone follow-up during recovery.

recommendations.section: Patient-centred care and shared decisions
recommendations.text: Use a needs-based palliative approach when appropriate, including symptom control, communication, advance-care planning, and psychosocial or spiritual support.
